vignette: Mara, a 65-year-old widowed woman of Oceania descent, works as a cybersecurity analyst. Her life was forever changed by a near-fatal car accident that left her with deep emotional and physical scars. The event occurred on a foggy night when she lost control of her vehicle and skidded off the road into a ravine. Although she survived, the trauma has haunted her ever since. Since the accident, Mara’s nights have been plagued by vivid images of the crash. When she closes her eyes, she can smell the scent of burning rubber and gasoline that permeated the air during the event. These olfactory memories trigger intense physical pain in her body, particularly in her right arm where she sustained a compound fracture. The recurrence of these visual and sensory memories has made it difficult for Mara to sleep soundly at night; every time she drifts off, she wakes up drenched in sweat, convinced that the same terrifying scenario might happen again. The memory of the accident has also led Mara to develop deep-seated negative appraisals about her body’s reliability. She is certain that her body cannot be trusted because it failed her during the crash, leaving her vulnerable and exposed. This belief exacerbates her feelings of injustice as she believes nothing has been done to rectify the unfairness of what happened to her. These thoughts have driven Mara into a cycle of rumination where she constantly goes over why the event occurred and how she could have prevented it. This persistent ruminating has led to further maladaptive strategies, including an almost obsessive need to avoid any situation that might trigger negative or positive feelings. She tries to erase the memory of the event entirely but finds herself trapped in a loop of replaying the crash over and over again. Her attempts at erasure only intensify her distress. The negative appraisals have also heightened Mara’s sense of vigilance, particularly at night when she feels most vulnerable. She often wakes up from a light sleep to check whether everything is still safe around her home. This constant need for reassurance has made it difficult for her to rest and has contributed significantly to her overall anxiety. Moreover, the memories of the accident have reinforced her feelings of being exposed to others. Mara believes that anyone who sees her can tell what she has been through just by looking at her—this sense of vulnerability further exacerbates her vigilance and leads her to avoid situations where she might be judged or seen as weak. Over time, these maladaptive strategies have affected Mara’s work as a cybersecurity analyst. She finds herself distracted during the day, constantly preoccupied with thoughts about the accident. Her heightened state of alertness has led to irritability at work, making it difficult for her to maintain focus and collaborate effectively with colleagues. This has strained her relationships both professionally and personally. The cumulative impact of these symptoms finally prompted Mara to seek help. What frightened her most was the relentless cycle she found herself in—her inability to escape the memories and negative thoughts that had taken over her life. She is hopeful that with support, she can regain a sense of control and trust in her own body again.
